title: Prefetch coordinator time-drift investigation notes
content:
Summary:
We observed a pattern of gradual memory amplification on multi-tenant hosts correlated with bursts of redundant prefetch activity. After initial triage, the strongest hypothesis is that an invisible time-drift window in the prefetch coordinator causes overlapping prefetch schedules across worker threads, producing duplicate KV cache prefetches and temporary peak memory that can push hosts toward OOM under medium load spikes.

Why this matters:
- Symptoms looked like intermittent OOMs and high alloc churn during sustained request bursts.
- Root cause differs from classic eviction or leak: the working set grows quickly during the burst then collapses once duplicate prefetches finish, leaving hosts susceptible to transient OOMs.
- This is reproducible and controllable in canary region if coordinator timing is manipulated, so actionable mitigation is possible without full runtime rewrite.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2025-10-28 03:42: oncall pager triggered for host-group us-west-2-gpu-5 (memory spike > 85%)
- 2025-10-28 03:43: SRE patched transient dynconfig to lower prefetch concurrency cap (quick mitigation)
- 2025-10-28 04:05: further spikes across two hosts, similar shape in allocation traces
- 2025-10-29 09:12: Diego ran targeted repro with clock skew injector and observed duplicate prefetch batches
- 2025-10-30 16:00: small experiment introduced 15s coordinator jitter on canary pool; peak duplicate prefetch count down ~40%

Key observations and signals:
- Allocation heatmap (runtimectl profile) shows repeated short-lived peaks aligned with prefetch job start times rather than sustained growth from leaks.
- Coordinator logs show multiple prefetch requests for the same tenant-key within an overlapping time window (log lines: prefetch.start id=..., prefetch.queue_delay=12ms).
- Host-level clock skew between worker containers ranged up to ~120ms during noisy GC cycles; combined with deterministic scheduling this created repeated overlaps.
- Eviction did free memory after the burst but not quickly enough to avoid OOM under tight headroom and medium-scale request bursts.

Repro steps used locally (notes):
1) Start serving-runtime local canary with two prefetch worker threads (--prefetch-workers=2).
2) Use clock injector to add 100-200ms drift to worker B (runtimectl debug-inject clock-drift workerB 150ms).
3) Run synthetic workload that triggers prefetch for long-context tenants (scripts/loadgen/prefetch-heavy.sh).
4) Observe allocator peaks via runtimectl profile and check logs for overlapping prefetch.start entries.

Interim mitigations applied in prod canary (fast, low-risk):
- Add small non-deterministic jitter to prefetch coordinator schedule (experiment: uniform[0,15s]). Result: duplicate prefetch count down ~40% in canary over 24h.
- Lower prefetch concurrency cap per-host from 12 -> 8 on impacted pools. This reduced peak memory but increases tail latency for some cold sequences.
- Add transient backpressure: when host memory > 78%, pause new prefetch jobs for 5s; this prevented one OOM in the following 48h window.

Longer-term fixes and engineering proposals:
1) Monotonic scheduling ticket: switch coordinator to use monotonic tick counters (avoid wall clock) and base scheduling windows on leader-assigned epochs. Benefits: robust to container-level clock jitter.
2) Dedup prevention: maintain small in-memory prefetch bloom filter keyed by tenant+seq-range within sliding window (configurable TTL). This avoids duplicate work without needing global coordination.
3) Dynamic TTL: tune prefetch TTL per-tenant by observed request patterns and memory headroom.
4) Graceful drain policy: when a host indicates soft memory pressure, proactively evict less-used prefetched KVs before admitting new prefetch jobs.
5) Observability: emit prefetch-id and dedup-hit metrics; add dashboard and alert when per-host dedup-rate > X% for Y minutes.

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Jitter reduces duplicates but can increase variance in prefetch readiness, possibly hurting tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants.
- Bloom filter dedup reduces memory waste but requires tuning of false-positive rate; too aggressive dedup may reduce hit rates for legitimate parallel prefetch needs.
- Monotonic ticks require coordinated rollout across runtime versions for correctness; partial rollouts could temporarily change scheduling semantics.

Immediate next steps (owners and ETA):
- (Anika) Draft RFC for monotonic scheduler and bloom dedup pattern. ETA: 2025-11-14.
- (Diego) Expand canary test with 10x longer run (7 days) with jitter enabled and capture dedup metrics. ETA: 2025-11-12.
- (Priya) Add prefetch.dedup_rate, prefetch.duplicate_jobs and prefetch.backpressure_events to monitoring and create an alert playbook. ETA: 2025-11-17.
- (SRE rotation) Continue runbook: if hosts show memory > 90% despite mitigations, scale down prefetch concurrency and escalate to eng-serving-runtime.

Open questions and items to validate:
- At what false-positive rate for the bloom filter do we start to materially degrade cache-warmth for high-concurrency tenants?
- Can monotonic tick change be accomplished with a rolling upgrade without coordination windows causing regressions?
- Are there other sources of timing overlap (e.g., leader elections, GC pauses) we missed? Need to instrument more finely.

Appendix: quick debugging commands used during investigation:
- kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=prefetch-coord -c coord --since=2h | grep prefetch.start
- runtimectl profile dump --since 2025-10-28T03:30:00Z --host us-west-2-gpu-5 > /tmp/profile.json
- runtimectl debug-inject clock-drift workerB 150ms
- scripts/loadgen/prefetch-heavy.sh --tenants 50 --rate 200

Notes to oncall:
- If you see repeated prefetch.start for same key within < 2s, consider toggling prefetch.jitter to smaller window or temporarily reducing prefetch.concurrency.
- When filing a follow-up incident ticket, include runtimectl profile snippet and prefetch.start log lines; this greatly speeds up triage.

Status: working hypothesis supported by canary experiments. Preparing RFC and longer canary run before implementing dedup filter in codebase.

-- Anika (oncall lead)
